Question Paper

  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SIXTH SEMESTER B.TECH. (COMPUTER SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING/ INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY) DEGREE  
  EXAMINATIONS - APRIL / MAY 2025  
  SUBJECT: HUM 3021/HUM_3021/HUM_3151 - ENGINEERING ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT  
Answer ALL the questions.  
Missing data may be suitably assumed.  
Interest factor tables are provided with question and in reference section, for others use formula.  
Formula book is provided in the reference section.  
  ENGINEERING ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT [HUM 3021]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               A loan of ₹20,000 requires monthly payments of ₹526 over a 48-month period of time. These                   (4)  
  payments include both principal and interest.  
  i) What is the nominal interest rate for this loan?  
  ii) What is the effective interest rate per year?  
  iii) Determine the amount of unpaid loan principal after 24 months.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)          The following data refers to the cash flows of five investment proposals. The total money available to the         (3)  
  company to invest is ₹35,000/-. The company can accept any one of the proposals with the same letter or  
  a combination of proposals with different letters subject to the budget available. Select the best alternative  
  based on the present worth of the total investment criterion. The rate of return is 10%.  
  
  
  Page 1 of 7

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
1C)   A working woman is planning for her retired life. She has 20 more years of service. She earns ₹50,000     (3)  
  per month. She would like to deposit 10% of her salary at the end of the first year and thereafter she  
  wishes to increase the deposit amount every year by ₹1,000 to the previous year for the next 14 years. At  
  an interest rate of 15%, estimate the total amount at the end of the 15 th year.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2A)       An industrial-grade asset was acquired for ₹5,00,000 to support critical production operations. It   (4)  
  has an expected useful life of 10 years, with a salvage value anticipated to be ₹1,00,000 at the end  
  of this period. Using the Declining Balance Depreciation Method, calculate the undepreciated  
  capital at the end of the 5 th year. Also, determine the depreciation charge for the 7th year.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)    Two assets, X and Y, are being considered for selection based on their ability to effectively perform a   (3)  
  required operational function, each with unique financial implications.  
  Asset Y requires an initial investment of Rs 34,000, with an anticipated salvage value of Rs 4,500 at the  
  end of a 4-year service life with operating expenses of Rs. 1,000 per year.  
  Asset X, on the other hand, has a lower initial cost, priced Rs 9,500 less than Y, yet has a shorter  
  economic lifespan by one year and no salvage value. Furthermore, X incurs additional annual operating  
  expenses of Rs 2,800 compared to Y. Given a required rate of return of 15%, using study period of 3  
  years, determine which asset offers the more favourable financial outcome. Assume, the market value  
  is equal to book value and assets depreciate according to straight line method.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2C)   Type 'A' bridge or Type 'B' bridge are under consideration which can be built as a part of a project for the   (3)  
  same purpose. The initial cost of a type A bridge is \$75,000 and the annual maintenance costs will  
  average \$400 per year and last forever. Type B bridge, which must be replaced every 30 years, will cost  
  \$40,000 to build and an annual maintenance cost of \$700. Both bridges have no salvage value. Using  
  capitalized cost approach with an interest rate is 6%, which alternative is to be selected?  
  
  
  Page 2 of 7

Additive B has a first cost of \$175,000 and an annual operating cost of \$35,000.  
  If the company uses a 3-year recovery period for paint products and a MARR of 20% per year,  
  which process is economically favoured? Use Incremental ROR analysis.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"

4A)   A car purchased six years ago for ₹5.50 lakhs by an ABC Ltd. can be sold now for ₹3.5 lakhs or can be (4)  
  kept for another five years. In that case, it will have an annual operation and maintenance cost of  
  ₹50,000 for the first year of operation from now and increases every year by an amount of 20,000. It is  
  expected to have a salvage value of ₹2.25 Lakhs, ₹2 Lakhs, ₹1.75 Lakhs, ₹1.5 Lakhs, ₹1.25 Lakhs for  
  years seven to eleven respectively. A suitable replacement a new car is priced at ₹8.25 Lakhs and an  
  annual operation and maintenance cost of ₹30,000. The salvage value of the new car is ₹5 Lakhs after  
  six years of its life. Evaluate and decide whether the old car can be replaced (Risk adjusted  
  $$MARR=10\%).$$  
  
  
  Page 4 of 7

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"

4C)   The manager of Erie Pvt. Ltd. is involved in a production planning process and wishes to conduct a (3)  
  risk assessment using two scenarios, the worst case and best-case scenarios, based on the  
  company's current estimated levels. Based on the following information about Erie Ltd, you must  
  conduct a break-even analysis under these scenarios. The manager adopts the pricing strategy that  
  involves determining the selling price of the product and then figuring out if it can be made at a cost  
  lower than that.  
  
  i) Under best case scenario the manager expects the selling price of ₹47,000, and the variable cost  
  of manufacturing the unit is ₹27,200. What could the company's fixed cost per year be to break  
  even with sales of 18,000 units per year?  
  
  ii) Under the worst-case scenario, the manager expects the selling price dropping to ₹36,000 and  
  variable cost increasing to ₹30,000, in this situation what would be the fixed cost per year to break  
  even if the sales remain unchanged at 18,000 units per year.  
  Based on the results of the break-even analysis for both the Best-Case and Worst-Case scenarios,  
  how do these help in the company's financial risk minimization and decision-making?  
  Page 5 of 7

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)         Why is the current ratio considered a key liquidity ratio in assessing a company's financial health?     (2)  
  How does it differ from the quick ratio, and why is the distinction important?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)   A frozen fish company is planning an expansion to a cold storage facility. Two alternative site design            (4)  
  proposals are being considered at an interest rate of 10% after consideration of risk in investments. Plant A  
  requires an expenditure of \$350,000 for land, while Plant B requires \$425,000. Assume that the land will be  
  sold after 30 years at the same purchase price. The buildings are expected to last 30 years, the  
  compressors and related equipment will last 10 years before requiring replacement. The annual  
  maintenance of the any compressor costs \$1,000 and increases by \$500 every year throughout the  
  compressor's life.  
  The energy costs of the facility are as given below and will increase throughout the building's life. Neither the  
  buildings nor the equipment is expected to have any salvage value. With this information and the data  
  provided below make an annual cost comparison to determine which proposal is preferred.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5C)      An equipment having a life of 15 years with an initial cost of \$12,100 is being considered for               (4)  
  replacement The salvage value of a one-year-old equipment is \$7,000 and this value then onwards  
  decreases every year by an amount of \$300.The maintenance and operating cost is \$1,200 in the first  
  year and then onwards it is expected to increase by \$1,000 every year in future years. Compute the  
  economic life of this asset and the minimum EUAC, with i=10%.
